audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers disagreed on five of seven rows. Full phases[].side read Neeko/Neeko/Skill/Skill/Neeko/Skill/Skill; content win[] and the packet levelChart both read Skill/Skill/Neeko/Skill/Ekko/Ekko/Ekko. The content whys also argued the opposite of their own win[] tokens on rows 0-1.
audit.why: Blooming Burst is 800 range on the same 9s cooldown as your Q at 1075 — level 1 is a genuine skill row, not hers. Tangle-Barbs arrives at 3 and is the row she owns. From 6 on, Chronobreak (110s) outlives Pop Blossom (120s) and Ekko wins 55.81% over 602 games.
audit.corrected: Full sides moved onto the content values: Skill/Skill/Neeko/Skill/Ekko/Ekko/Ekko, with every flipped why rewritten in the same proposal, plus whys[0], whys[1] and whys[3] rewritten to stop contradicting their own rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was written as Neeko's row on the full layer while the content layer called it yours, and no spike named a cooldown.
audit.why: Pop Blossom is 120/105/90s and needs a preparation window before the leap; Chronobreak is 110/80/50s and scales down twice as fast, so the ultimate trade swings further your way every rank.
audit.corrected: Level 6 is now yours on both layers, and the spike text keys off the 120s versus 110s gap and the fact that Pop Blossom's wind-up is only hidden while she is disguised.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page named a Neeko ability except the focus token, and the decisive interactions were missing: Tangle-Barbs grows larger, faster and longer-rooting after it passes through any champion or kills a unit, and Inherent Glamour's disguise breaks on immobilizing crowd control.
audit.why: enemyKit E text: passing through a champion or killing an enemy makes the tangle bigger, faster and root longer. enemyKit P text: receiving immobilizing crowd control, casting damaging spells, or the disguise taking its healthbar in damage breaks it.
audit.corrected: The page now states that a Tangle-Barbs that clips a minion wave arrives upgraded, so you dodge from behind the caster minions rather than beside them, and that your W stun breaks her disguise outright.
sources: brief enemyKit E and P text

audit.why: It is the field that carries real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Now carries Tangle-Barbs 12s at rank 1 down to 10s, Blooming Burst 9s, Pop Blossom 120s, Chronobreak 110s.

edits.before: Neeko's biggest early threat is her root — if she lands it, she gets a free full combo on you with almost no counterplay once it connects. Levels 1-2 stay cautious and vary your walk pattern so she can't time an easy root; her disguise passive also means random minions or wards could be her, so play a bit more paranoid than usual. Levels 3-5 remain her lane to press since her burst-on-root combo out-trades your kit before you have combo damage online — bait the root from max range rather than trading blind.
edits.after: Neeko's biggest early threat is Tangle-Barbs — landed, it roots long enough for the whole rotation, and it roots longer still once it has passed through a minion or champion on the way. Levels 1-2 are genuinely even: she has no root yet and your Q reaches 1075 to Blooming Burst's 800, so take the poke war. Level 3 is hers, and levels 4-5 come back to even because Tangle-Barbs is 12s at rank 1 — dodge from behind the caster minions, then take the gap.

edits.before: Level 6 flips this matchup meaningfully: Chronobreak's healing and reposition let you survive a landed root-combo that would otherwise kill you outright, and punish her for over-extending the all-in. Keep playing around wards and vision to catch her disguise plays before they land — a spotted Neeko loses most of her power. Once her root is on cooldown or she's committed it on a decoy/minion, that's your window to all-in with Q-E-AA before she can reset the trade.
edits.after: Level 6 flips this matchup on the cooldown maths: Chronobreak is 110s to Pop Blossom's 120s, so you get the rewind back sooner than she gets the leap, and a landed root that would have killed you outright becomes a survivable one. Keep buying vision — the leap's wind-up is only hidden while she is disguised, so a spotted Neeko loses the ambush entirely. Once Tangle-Barbs is spent on a minion, that 12s is your window for Q-E-AA.

notes: Five of seven chart rows disagreed across layers here, and the content whys additionally argued against their own win[] tokens on rows 0-1 (win[0]/win[1] said Skill while whys[0]/whys[1] described Neeko owning both). I moved the full layer onto the content values, which match the packet levelChart, and rewrote every affected why on both layers in this one proposal; win[] itself needed no edit because it already held the correct tokens. Load-bearing facts that were entirely absent from the page and are now on it: Tangle-Barbs upgrades (bigger, faster, longer root) after passing a champion or killing a unit, and Inherent Glamour breaks on immobilizing crowd control, which Ekko's W anomaly stun is. Left unwritten because the kits do not answer it: whether the W stun catches Neeko during Pop Blossom's airborne frames, and whether Shapesplitter clones can trigger the anomaly.
